answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring every new identity to post a bond before it may receive valuable tasks. Verifiers randomly assign overlapping work to agents, while a violet challenge can expose inconsistent answers; a zephyr of low-cost identities gains nothing because colluding agents must risk separate deposits. If one identity lies or coordinates conflicting reports, the protocol uses the anchor record of prior commitments to slash its bond and reduce its future task share, making each Sybil expensive rather than free.
